claims.source: The subsequent wave, known as definitive, produces: first, oligopotent erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMPs) in the YS (E8-E8.5); and later myelo-lymphoid progenitors (MLPs – E9.5-E10), multipotent progenitors (MPPs – E10-E11.5), and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs – E10.5-E11.5), in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) region of the embryo proper (Ivanovs et al., 2011; McGrath et al., 2015; Palis et al., 1999; Medvinsky and Dzierzak, 1996; Medvinsky et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are produced at E10.5-E11.5 in the AGM region.
claims.source: The subsequent wave, known as definitive, produces: first, oligopotent erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMPs) in the YS (E8-E8.5); and later myelo-lymphoid progenitors (MLPs – E9.5-E10), multipotent progenitors (MPPs – E10-E11.5), and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs – E10.5-E11.5), in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros (AGM) region of the embryo proper (Ivanovs et al., 2011; McGrath et al., 2015; Palis et al., 1999; Medvinsky and Dzierzak, 1996; Medvinsky et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Definitive blood waves are characteristically specified from a specialized HE through a process of endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT).
claims.source: Definitive blood waves are characteristically specified from a specialized HE through a process of endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT) (Zovein et al., 2008; Li et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: HSC specification from HE is the last event in hematopoietic development and occurs in characteristic cell clusters found on the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta.
claims.source: HSC specification from HE is the last event in hematopoietic development and occurs in characteristic cell clusters found on the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta (Ivanovs et al., 2011; Boisset et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: All blood cell types enter circulation from their original locations and migrate to the fetal liver (FL).
claims.source: All blood cell types enter circulation from their original locations and migrate to the fetal liver (FL) (Ciriza et al., 2013; Ghiaur et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Most embryonic blood progenitors are transient and sustain blood production exclusively during embryonic development, through differentiation.
claims.source: Most embryonic blood progenitors are transient and sustain blood production exclusively during embryonic development, through differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field of embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: HSCs make little or no contribution to embryonic and fetal blood; instead, they proliferate (i.e. self-renew) to expand their numbers.
claims.source: In contrast, HSCs make little or no contribution to embryonic and fetal blood; instead, they proliferate (i.e. self-renew) to expand their numbers.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field of embryonic hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: At least a subset of HSCs migrates to the bone marrow (BM) niche at the end of gestation and balances self-renewal and differentiation to maintain blood production throughout the entire post-natal life.
claims.source: At least a subset of HSCs migrates to the bone marrow (BM) niche at the end of gestation and balances self-renewal and differentiation to maintain blood production throughout the entire post-natal life (Bowie et al., 2006; Kikuchi and Kondo, 2006; Ganuza et al., 2022; Yokomizo et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on HSC biology.

claims.claim: Leukemia is the most common malignancy and the most common cause of cancer-related death in the pediatric age group.
claims.source: Leukemia is the most common malignancy and the most common cause of cancer-related death in the pediatric age group (Steliarova-Foucher et al., 2017; Dong et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on pediatric cancer epidemiology.

claims.claim: Several pediatric leukemias originate in utero.
claims.source: Several pediatric leukemias originate in utero, and a subset of these are driven by mutations exclusive to the pediatric group (Masetti et al., 2015; Cazzola et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on pediatric leukemia.

claims.claim: A subset of pediatric leukemias are driven by mutations exclusive to the pediatric group.
claims.source: Several pediatric leukemias originate in utero, and a subset of these are driven by mutations exclusive to the pediatric group (Masetti et al., 2015; Cazzola et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on pediatric leukemia.

claims.claim: Pediatric-exclusive mutations target blood cell types restricted to development or depend on signals that are specific to embryonic hematopoietic niches.
claims.source: Such pediatric-exclusive mutations target blood cell types restricted to development or depend on signals that are specific to embryonic hematopoietic niches, effectively defining distinct biological entities to adult malignancies (Cazzola et al., 2020; Bolouri et al., 2018; Chaudhury et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on pediatric leukemia.

claims.claim: t(7;12) (q36;p13) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by rearrangement and overexpression of the MNX1 gene locus.
claims.source: One such example is t(7;12) (q36;p13) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) driven by rearrangement and overexpression of the MNX1 gene locus: MNX1-rearranged (MNX1-r) AML is restricted to infants under the age of 2 and carries a high risk of relapse and poor survival (Ragusa et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on MNX1-rearranged AML.

claims.claim: MNX1-rearranged (MNX1-r) AML is restricted to infants under the age of 2.
claims.source: One such example is t(7;12) (q36;p13) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) driven by rearrangement and overexpression of the MNX1 gene locus: MNX1-rearranged (MNX1-r) AML is restricted to infants under the age of 2 and carries a high risk of relapse and poor survival (Ragusa et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on MNX1-rearranged AML.

claims.claim: MNX1-rearranged (MNX1-r) AML carries a high risk of relapse and poor survival.
claims.source: One such example is t(7;12) (q36;p13) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) driven by rearrangement and overexpression of the MNX1 gene locus: MNX1-rearranged (MNX1-r) AML is restricted to infants under the age of 2 and carries a high risk of relapse and poor survival (Ragusa et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on MNX1-rearranged AML.

claims.claim: MNX1 is a developmental gene required for specification of motor neurons and pancreatic acinar cells.
claims.source: MNX1 is a developmental gene required for specification of motor neurons and pancreatic acinar cells (Thaler et al., 1999; Harrison et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on MNX1 function.

claims.claim: MNX1 is not known to participate in embryonic hematopoiesis.
claims.source: MNX1 is not known to participate in embryonic hematopoiesis; however, it has been discordantly described to be expressed in some subsets of adult hematopoietic cells (Deguchi and Kehrl, 1991; Nagel et al., 2005; Wildenhain et al., 2012; Taketani et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the absence of evidence in the literature for MNX1 function in embryonic hematopoiesis, as indicated by the citations.

claims.claim: MNX1 has been discordantly described to be expressed in some subsets of adult hematopoietic cells.
claims.source: MNX1 is not known to participate in embryonic hematopoiesis; however, it has been discordantly described to be expressed in some subsets of adult hematopoietic cells (Deguchi and Kehrl, 1991; Nagel et al., 2005; Wildenhain et al., 2012; Taketani et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on MNX1 expression.

claims.claim: MNX1 is ectopically expressed in AML cells carrying one of a variable set of t(7;12) translocations which place the normally silent MNX1 gene under the control of ETV6 regulatory elements.
claims.source: It is ectopically expressed in AML cells carrying one of a variable set of t(7;12) translocations which place the normally silent MNX1 gene under the control of ETV6 regulatory elements (Weichenhan et al., 2023; Bousquets-Muñoz et al., 2024; Ragusa et al., 2023; Ballabio et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on MNX1-rearranged AML.

claims.claim: ETV6 is required for hematopoietic cell specification from HE via VEGF signalling.
claims.source: ETV6 is required for hematopoietic cell specification from HE via VEGF signalling (Ciau-Uitz et al., 2010), potentially positioning MNX1 within a critical embryonic hemogenic regulatory network.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on ETV6 function.

claims.claim: Gastruloid models have emerged as robust avatars of early development, self-organizing processes of symmetry breaking, elongation, multi-axis formation, somitogenesis and early organogenesis, with remarkable similarity to embryo processes in space and time.
claims.source: In the last few years, gastruloid models have emerged as robust avatars of early development, self-organizing processes of symmetry breaking, elongation, multi-axis formation, somitogenesis and early organogenesis, with remarkable similarity to embryo processes in space and time (van den Brink and van Oudenaarden, 2021; Beccari et al., 2018; van den Brink et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on gastruloid models.

claims.claim: A variant gastruloid culture system was able to recapitulate YS blood formation with erythroid and myeloid cellularity.
claims.source: Relevant to blood formation, a variant gastruloid culture system, which successfully organizes a heart primordium (Rossi et al., 2021), was also able to recapitulate YS blood formation with erythroid and myeloid cellularity (Rossi et al., 2021; Rossi et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on gastruloid models of hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: The haemGx protocol includes an indispensable pulse of Activin A to induce hemato-endothelial programmes via TGF-β signalling.
claims.source: The haemGx protocol includes an indispensable pulse of Activin A to induce hemato-endothelial programmes via TGF-β signalling (visible by proxy of GFP-tagged Flk1 activation), in addition to the characteristic gastruloid patterning via WNT activation by CHI99021 supplementation at 48 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that Activin A is required for Flk1-GFP activation and subsequent hematopoietic development.

claims.claim: Hemato-endothelial programs were promoted through addition of VEGF and FGF2 at 72 hr.
claims.source: We promoted hemato-endothelial programs through addition of VEGF and FGF2 at 72 hr (Sroczynska et al., 2009; Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior literature on hematopoietic differentiation.

claims.claim: A polarized Flk1-GFP-expressing branched endothelial network was observed in haemGx.
claims.source: We observed extension of a polarized Flk1-GFP-expressing branched endothelial network (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing Flk1-GFP expression in haemGx.

claims.claim: Flow cytometry analysis revealed the onset of VE-cadherin+ C-Kit+ cells suggestive of EHT, with a peak at 120–144 hr.
claims.source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed the onset of VE-cadherin+ C-Kit+ cells suggestive of EHT, with a peak at 120–144 hr (Figure 1C–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing the time-dependent appearance of VE-cadherin+ C-Kit+ cells.

claims.claim: A surge in CD41+ candidate hematopoietic cells was observed at 144 hr in haemGx.
claims.source: This was followed by a surge in CD41+ candidate hematopoietic cells at 144 hr (Figure 1C–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing the time-dependent appearance of CD41+ cells.

claims.claim: A 24 hr pulse of sonic hedgehog (Shh) between 144–168 hr was incorporated to mimic the aortic patterning that precedes cluster formation.
claims.source: We incorporated a 24 hr pulse of sonic hedgehog (Shh) between 144–168 hr to mimic the aortic patterning that precedes cluster formation (Figure 1A; Rybtsov et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental design and citation to prior literature on HSC development.

claims.claim: Continued exposure to VEGF after the Shh pulse resulted in specification of CD45+ hematopoietic cells progenitors.
claims.source: Continued exposure to VEGF after the Shh pulse resulted in specification of CD45+ hematopoietic cells progenitors (Figure 1C–E), which were apparent after 168 hr.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing the time-dependent appearance of CD45+ cells.

claims.claim: The proportion of CD45+ cells was enhanced by the addition of SCF, FLT3L, and TPO.
claims.source: The proportion of CD45+ cells was enhanced by the addition of SCF, FLT3L, and TPO (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D), a combination of cytokines routinely used for HSC maintenance; conversely, it did not require continued addition of FGF2 after 168 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), which was omitted.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data comparing CD45+ cell frequencies with and without SCF, FLT3L, and TPO.

claims.claim: CD45+ cells were present in a small number of 'cluster'-like structures adjacent to Flk1-GFP+ Kit+ endothelium.
claims.source: CD45+ cells, some of which co-expressed C-Kit, were present in a small number of 'cluster'-like structures adjacent to Flk1-GFP+ Kit+ endothelium (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data showing the spatial organization of CD45+ cells.

claims.claim: Time-dependent specification of C-Kit+, CD41+, and CD45+ cells in haemGx could be obtained with other mouse ES cell lines, including commonly used E14Tg2a (E14) cells.
claims.source: Time-dependent specification of C-Kit+, CD41+, and CD45+ cells in haemGx could be obtained with other mouse ES cell lines, including commonly used E14Tg2a (E14) cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F-H), with successful specification of comparable frequencies of CD45+ progenitors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I), attesting to the reproducibility of the protocol across cell lines of different genetic backgrounds.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data from haemGx generated from different ES cell lines.

claims.claim: Endothelial identity of Flk1-GFP+ populations was detectable by flow cytometry through the presence of endothelial markers CD31 and CD34.
claims.source: Endothelial identity of Flk1-GFP+ populations was also detectable by flow cytometry through the presence of endothelial markers CD31 and CD34 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing co-expression of Flk1-GFP with CD31 and CD34.

claims.claim: Subsets of CD41+ and CD45+ hematopoietic cells co-express CD31 and CD34.
claims.source: Given the co-expression of CD31 and CD34 with hematopoietic progenitors emerging from HE, we inspected CD41+ and CD45+ cells for the presence of these markers. Indeed, we found that subsets of CD41+ and CD45+ hematopoietic cells co-express CD31 and CD34 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D), with increased relative representation of hemato-endothelial markers within CD41+ cells at 144 hr and CD45+ at 216 hr (Figure 2C), consistent with two successive waves of hemogenic emergence from HE.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing co-expression of hemato-endothelial markers.

claims.claim: CD45+ cells from 216 hr haemGx co-expressed C-Kit, Flk1-GFP, and VE-cadherin, a phenotype enriched in emergent hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) in the AGM.
claims.source: CD45+ cells from 216 hr haemGx also co-expressed C-Kit, Flk1-GFP, and VE-cadherin, a phenotype enriched in emergent hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) in the AGM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data and citation to prior literature on HSPC phenotypes.

claims.claim: The phenotype CD45+ C-Kit+ Flk1-GFP+ VE-cadherin+ is detected in 1.8% of CD45+ cells on average, corresponding to an estimated 8 cells per haemGx.
claims.source: The phenotype is detected in 1.8% of CD45+ cells on average (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G), corresponding to an estimated 8 cells per haemGx.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data quantifying the frequency of this phenotype.

claims.claim: Analysis of the haemGx progenitor content at 216 hr using multipotential CFC assays revealed the presence of >50 CFC/haemGx, of which an average of seven have mixed-lineage granulocytic-monocytic-erythroid (GEM) potential.
claims.source: In agreement, analysis of the haemGx progenitor content at 216 hr using multipotential CFC assays (Figure 2D–E) revealed the presence of >50 CFC/haemGx, of which an average of seven have mixed-lineage granulocytic-monocytic-erythroid (GEM) potential, numerically matching the estimated number of HSPC.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by CFC assay data quantifying colony-forming potential.

claims.claim: Other progenitors in haemGx were predominantly granulo-monocytic (GM) and erythroid (E) progenitors.
claims.source: Other progenitors were predominantly granulo-monocytic (GM) and erythroid (E) progenitors (Figure 2D–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by CFC assay data showing the types of colonies formed.

claims.claim: Analysis of the cellularity of dissociated haemGx at the 216 hr timepoint using Giemsa-Wright stained cytospins revealed differentiated cells of G, M, E, and megakaryocytic lineages.
claims.source: Analysis of the cellularity of dissociated haemGx at the 216 hr timepoint using Giemsa-Wright stained cytospins revealed differentiated cells of G, M, E, and megakaryocytic lineages (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), putatively reflecting the progeny of EMP-like cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cytospin analysis showing differentiated cell morphologies.

claims.claim: Temporal progression of expression of key markers was observed by qPCR, configuring a sustained hemato-endothelial program from 120 hr through 216 hr.
claims.source: We observed temporal progression of expression of key markers by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR), configuring a sustained hemato-endothelial program from 120 hr through 216 hr (Dll4 and Mecom), and the generation of hematopoietic populations based on the time-dependent patterns of Myb, Runx1, Hlf, and Hoxa9 (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data showing time-dependent gene expression patterns.

claims.claim: Myb peaks at 144 hr, coincident with the emergence of CD41+ cells, which are postulated to have YS-like EMP characteristics.
claims.source: We note that Myb peaks at 144 hr, coincident with the emergence of CD41+ cells, which we postulate to have YS-like EMP characteristics.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data showing Myb expression and inference from the timing of CD41+ cell emergence.

claims.claim: Runx1 has a bimodal pattern peaking at 144 hr, and later at 216 hr, suggesting the presence of two distinct hematopoietic waves.
claims.source: On the other hand, Runx1 has a bimodal pattern peaking at 144 hr, and later at 216 hr, suggesting the presence of two distinct hematopoietic waves.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data showing Runx1 expression and inference from the bimodal pattern.

claims.claim: The later timepoint of 216 hr has significantly higher expression of both Hoxa9 and Hlf raising the possibility that the second wave corresponds to the specification of AGM-like HSPC.
claims.source: The later timepoint of 216 hr has significantly higher expression of both Hoxa9 and Hlf raising the possibility that the second wave indeed corresponds to the specification of AGM-like HSPC.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data showing Hoxa9 and Hlf expression and inference from their association with AGM hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Upon EZH2 inhibition via treatment with GSK216 from 120 hr onwards, a reduction of CD41+ cells was observed selectively at 144 hr, with no change in CD45+ cells at the later timepoint of 216 hr.
claims.source: Upon EZH2 inhibition via treatment with GSK216 from 120 hr onwards, we observed a reduction of CD41+ cells selectively at 144 hr, with no change in CD45+ cells at the later timepoint of 216 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data comparing CD41+ and CD45+ cell frequencies with and without EZH2 inhibitor.

claims.claim: The vulnerability of 144 hr CD41+ to EZH2 inhibition suggests that they include YS-like EMP and do not predominantly reflect EZH2-independent primitive YS hematopoiesis.
claims.source: This suggests that the cells present at the later timepoint may not be the progeny of the former, thus supporting recapitulation of two independent hematopoietic waves, the latter putatively AGM. Additionally, the vulnerability of 144 hr CD41+ to EZH2 inhibition suggests that they include YS-like EMP and do not predominantly reflect EZH2-independent primitive YS hematopoiesis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the EZH2 inhibition data and citation to prior literature on EZH2 function in hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing time-course analysis of haemGx cell specification was performed, profiling a total of 846 cells using the Smart-Seq2 protocol.
claims.source: We sorted cells from two independent haemGx cultures at 120, 144, 168, 192, and 216 hr, and profiled a total of 846 cells using the Smart-Seq2 protocol (Picelli et al., 2014; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the scRNA-seq experimental design and citation to the Smart-Seq2 protocol.

claims.claim: Library preparation and sequencing generated an average of 120,000 reads/cell, which were mapped to an average of 4000 genes/cell.
claims.source: Library preparation and sequencing generated an average of 120,000 reads/cell, which were mapped to an average of 4000 genes/cell, with minimal signs of cell stress/death as measured by mitochondrial DNA fraction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quality control metrics from the scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: 12 cell clusters were identified in the scRNA-seq analysis, of which 2 (clusters 0 and 5) almost exactly mapped to C-Kit+ cells, 2 (clusters 1 and 8) contained CD45+ sorted cells, and cluster 4 uniquely captured the CD41+ cells observed at 144 hr.
claims.source: We identified 12 cell clusters of which 2 (clusters 0 and 5) almost exactly mapped to C-Kit+ cells (also positive for Sca-1), 2 (clusters 1 and 8) contained CD45+ sorted cells, and cluster 4 uniquely captured the CD41+ cells observed at 144 hr (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq clustering analysis and mapping to sorted cell populations.

claims.claim: Top classifier genes for clusters 0 and 5 had endothelial affiliation.
claims.source: Top classifier genes for clusters 0 and 5 had endothelial affiliation (Supplementary file 1 and Supplementary file 2), and the cellular composition of the clusters broadly reflected their time signature (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D): cluster 5 comprised 144 hr cells and cluster 0 included most C-Kit+ cells at 192 hr.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Cluster 5 occupied the vicinity of 144 hr CD41+ cells, which carried an erythroid-biased signature.
claims.source: Cluster 5 occupied the vicinity of 144 hr CD41+ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), which carried an erythroid-biased signature (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq clustering analysis and gene expression signatures.

claims.claim: 192/216h-CD45+ cells in cluster 8 expressed myeloid and lymphoid genes.
claims.source: On the other hand, 192/216h-CD45+ cells in cluster 8 expressed myeloid and lymphoid genes (Supplementary file 1 and Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claims.claim: Clusters of cells present at later timepoints matched mesenchymal stromal cell and autonomic neuron signatures, potentially configuring incipient formation of niches relevant to production of HSCs.
claims.source: The remaining clusters largely corresponded to time-restricted unfractionated cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, bottom panel), with clusters of cells present at later timepoints matching mesenchymal stromal cell and autonomic neuron signatures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), potentially configuring incipient formation of niches relevant to production of HSCs (Kapeni et al., 2022; Fitch et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cell type enrichment analysis of scRNA-seq data and citation to prior literature on HSC niches.

claims.claim: Pecam, Cd34, and Mecom expression coincided with clusters 0 and 3, which capture C-Kit+ cells at 144 and 192 hr, respectively.
claims.source: We observed a coincidence of Pecam, Cd34, and Mecom expression with clusters 0 and 3, which capture C-Kit+ cells at 144 and 192 hr, respectively.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: CD41+ and CD45+-sorted clusters show expression of Runx1, confirming their hematopoietic affiliation.
claims.source: CD41+ and CD45+-sorted clusters, on the other hand, show expression of Runx1, confirming their hematopoietic affiliation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: Cd44 is detected predominantly in C-Kit+-enriched cluster 3 and CD45+-sorted clusters 1 and 4, corresponding to the later timepoints of 192 and 216 hr.
claims.source: Cd44, which is upregulated at the endothelial-to-hematopoietic transition (EHT) and in association with the AGM region (Oatley et al., 2020; Fadlullah et al., 2022), is detected predominantly in C-Kit+-enriched cluster 3 and CD45+-sorted clusters 1 and 4, corresponding to the later timepoints of 192 and 216 hr.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and citation to prior literature on Cd44 function.

claims.claim: Significant increases in expression of VE-cadherin (Cdh5), Sox17, as well as Cd34, Cd44, and Procr were observed in 192 hr, endothelial-enriched, C-Kit+ cells.
claims.source: This supports the notion that the later timepoints may capture AGM-like EHT, which is also suggested by significant increases in expression of VE-cadherin (Cdh5), Sox17, as well as Cd34, Cd44, and Procr (Fadlullah et al., 2022; Frankish et al., 2019; Oatley et al., 2020) in 192 hr, endothelial-enriched, C-Kit+ cells (Figure 3C–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and citation to prior literature on AGM markers.

claims.claim: 192 hr C-Kit+ cells express arterial endothelial markers, including Flt1, Efnb2, and Dll4 steadily at both timepoints.
claims.source: Important in this context, these cells express arterial endothelial markers, including Flt1, Efnb2, and Dll4 steadily at both timepoints (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: Hoxa9 expression is detected exclusively in C-Kit and CD45-sorted cells in the 192 and 216 hr-timepoints of haemGx differentiation.
claims.source: Hoxa9 expression also associates with arterial specification and definitive AGM-like hematopoiesis: albeit at low frequency, it is detected exclusively in C-Kit and CD45-sorted cells in the 192 and 216 hr-timepoints of haemGx differentiation (Figure 3B and E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Hoxa9 also express Mllt3 and, rarely, Hlf, compatible with incipient specification of an AGM-like definitive blood program.
claims.source: These cells also express Mllt3 and, rarely, Hlf, compatible with incipient specification of an AGM-like definitive blood program (Figure 3B and E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and inference from the association of these genes with AGM hematopoiesis.

claims.claim: Mllt3 is additionally expressed in CD41+-sorted cells of cluster 2, in line with its role in early erythroid and megakaryocytic lineage identity.
claims.source: Mllt3 is additionally expressed in CD41+-sorted cells of cluster 2, in line with its role in early erythroid and megakaryocytic lineage identity (Pina et al., 2008); Myb is also more frequently expressed in this population (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and citation to prior literature on Mllt3 function.

claims.claim: Ikzf1 gradually increases its expression, and indeed frequency, in 216 hr-CD45+ sorted cells.
claims.source: In contrast, Ikzf1, which regulates lymphoid specification (Huang et al., 2019), gradually increases its expression, and indeed frequency, in 216 hr-CD45+ sorted cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and citation to prior literature on Ikzf1 function.

claims.claim: A handover from erythroid/megakaryocytic to myelo-lymphoid lineage affiliation is apparent between 144 hr and 216 hr haemGx blood cells.
claims.source: A handover from erythroid/megakaryocytic to myelo-lymphoid lineage affiliation is apparent between 144 hr and 216 hr haemGx blood cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis showing changes in lineage-affiliated gene expression.

claims.claim: A small number of erythroid-affiliated cells at 216 hr express adult globins, suggesting a definitive origin.
claims.source: Of note, a small number of erythroid-affiliated cells at 216 hr express adult globins, suggesting a definitive origin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis and inference from the expression of adult globins.

claims.claim: Projections of haemGx scRNA-seq data onto Hou et al., 2020 positioned clusters 0 and 3, corresponding to endothelium, including arterial endothelium and HE-like cells, between days E8.5 and E10.
claims.source: Projections onto Hou et al., 2020 positioned clusters 0 and 3, corresponding to endothelium, including arterial endothelium and HE-like cells, between days E8.5 and E10, putatively spanning YS-like and AGM-like blood formation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by projection analysis of scRNA-seq data onto published embryonic datasets.

claims.claim: A subset of CD45+-sorted cells, as well as a small numbers of CD41+ cells from cluster 2 projected onto E10 HE and intra-aortic cluster (IAC) cells, suggesting the presence of definitive HSPC or their precursors in haemGx.
claims.source: A subset of CD45+-sorted cells, as well as a small numbers of CD41+ cells from cluster 2 projected onto E10 HE and intra-aortic cluster (IAC) cells, suggesting the presence of definitive HSPC or their precursors in haemGx (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by projection analysis of scRNA-seq data onto published embryonic datasets.

claims.claim: A large proportion of CD41+-sorted cells matched the identity of YS EMP when projected onto Zhu et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Transplantation of dissociated haemGx cells obtained at 192 and 216 hr into irradiated immunocompetent C57Bl/6 recipients, sub-lethally irradiated immunodeficient NSG mice, or non-conditioned NSGW41 hosts failed to detect signs of engraftment.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from transplantation experiments.

claims.claim: Implantation of undissociated haemGx in the adrenal gland of Nude mice was tested to support further 3D maturation in vivo.
claims.source: We thus tested implantation of undissociated haemGx in the adrenal gland of Nude mice (Figure 4B), a topography more commonly used to support tumor development, but that was recently shown to be able to support HSC development, possibly with contributions from the sympathetic adrenal medullary niche (Schyrr et al., 2023).

claims.claim: Forms of AML unique to the first 2 years of life – infant (inf)AML – have been shown to transform fetal liver (FL) but not adult hematopoietic cells.
claims.source: In particular, forms of AML unique to the first 2 years of life – infant (inf)AML – have been shown to transform fetal liver (FL) but not adult hematopoietic cells (Waraky et al., 2024; Mercher et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2011; Ragusa et al., 2023), compatible with targeting of a transient embryonic cell.

claims.source: In the case of t(7;12) AML (herein MNX1-r) (Ragusa et al., 2023), in which the translocation results in transformation-driving ectopic expression of MNX1 (Waraky et al., 2024), analysis of patient transcriptional signatures (Ragusa et al., 2022) for over-representation of cell atlas-defined affiliations, indicates enrichment in cardiomyogenic, endothelial, HSC/progenitor, and mast cells (Figure 5A).

claims.source: We observed a small but significant expansion of the C-Kit+ compartment specifically at 144 hr (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).

claims.claim: DEGs between MNX1-OE and EV configured distinct MNX1-driven programs at 144 hr and 216 hr, with >80% genes timepoint-specific.
claims.source: DEGs between MNX1-OE and EV (Supplementary file 4) configured distinct MNX1-driven programs at 144 hr and 216 hr, with >80% genes timepoint-specific (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis comparing MNX1-OE and EV haemGx at different timepoints.

claims.claim: Both programs include up-regulation of hematopoietic-associated genes, capturing EHT and progenitor regulators at the earlier timepoint, and more differentiated effectors at 216 hr.
claims.source: Both programs include up-regulation of hematopoietic-associated genes, capturing EHT and progenitor regulators (e.g. Runx1, and Epor and Zfpm1, respectively) at the earlier timepoint, and more differentiated effectors, e.g., Hba-a1, Hbb-bh1, and Il3ra at 216 hr, compatible with selective targeting and/or expansion of YS EMP-like cells and their later differentiated progeny (Figure 5H).

claims.source: An overview of transcriptional regulatory programs at both timepoints denotes a clearer hemogenic enrichment at 144 hr, with over-representation of GATA2, GATA1r and RUNX1 binding targets (Figure 5I), putatively capturing an expansion of a HE-to-EMP-like transition, also represented in enriched GO categories related to VEGF signalling and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Figure 5J).

claims.source: Significantly, clusters 5 and 0 HE signatures were also enriched in MNX1-r infAML patient signatures (Ragusa et al., 2022; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C), putatively aligning MNX1-OE effects with HE and the hemogenic transition.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis of patient transcriptomes against haemGx cluster signatures.

claims.claim: Both 144 hr and 216 hr MNX1-OE haemGx replated for at least five platings and were significantly different to control (EV).
claims.source: Both 144 hr (Figure 6A–B) and 216 hr (Figure 6C–D) MNX1-OE haemGx replated for at least five platings were significantly different to control (EV) (Figure 6B and D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by serial replating assay data comparing MNX1-OE and EV haemGx.

claims.source: HsMNX1 reads were increased in MNX1-OE CFC samples, supporting selective expansion of transduced cells (Figure 7A).

claims.source: Cluster k14 had significant enrichment of MNX1-r signatures against all other AML subtypes (Figure 7C), with considerable overlap between leading-edge (i.e. significantly-enriched) genes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).

claims.source: Importantly, k14 captures the subgroup of DEGs up-regulated upon CFC replating which are also up-regulated in MNX1-OE haemGx at 144 hr (Figure 7B), matching the time-dependent enrichment of the putative MNX1-OE propagating population.

claims.source: The most highly significant signatures capture early developmental hemogenic components, such as 'endothelial cells' and 'erythroid cell precursors,' reflecting the 144 hr, putative YS affiliation of MNX1-OE haemGx.

claims.source: Giemsa-Wright-stained cytospins of serially replated CFC assays initiated with 144 hr MNX1-OE cells showed a shift from blast-like at plate 3 to precursor cell morphology with some differentiated mast cells at plate 5 (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cytospin analysis of serially replated cells.

claims.claim: Mast cells were also observed in 216 hr-initiated colonies, but these were differentiated at an earlier plate, suggesting that MNX1-OE-responsive C-Kit+ progenitors experience maturation between 144 hr and 216 hr.
claims.source: We also observed mast cells in 216 hr-initiated colonies (Figure 7E), but these were differentiated at an earlier plate, suggesting that MNX1-OE-responsive C-Kit+ progenitors experience maturation between 144 hr and 216 hr.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cytospin analysis of serially replated cells and inference from the timing of mast cell differentiation.

results.result: Current in vitro models of developmental blood formation lack spatio-temporal accuracy and weakly replicate successive waves of hematopoiesis.
results.evaluation: This claim (C1) represents established knowledge in the field and serves as motivation for the study. It is supported by the general understanding that existing models do not adequately capture the complexity of embryonic hematopoiesis, as evidenced by the need for the haemGx model developed in this manuscript.

results.result: The manuscript provides background on embryonic hematopoiesis, describing the first wave producing unipotent precursors in the yolk sac at E7-E7.5, followed by definitive waves producing EMPs, MLPs, MPPs, and HSCs in the AGM region at specific developmental timepoints, with HSCs ultimately migrating to the bone marrow.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C18 represent well-established knowledge in the field of embryonic hematopoiesis, supported by multiple citations to prior literature. These claims provide essential background context for understanding the haemGx model and are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: The manuscript provides background on pediatric leukemias, particularly MNX1-rearranged AML, which is restricted to infants under age 2, carries poor prognosis, and is driven by ectopic MNX1 expression under ETV6 regulatory control.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C30 represent established knowledge about pediatric leukemia and MNX1-rearranged AML, supported by citations to prior literature. These claims provide essential background for the disease modeling experiments but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Gastruloid models have emerged as robust avatars of early development with remarkable similarity to embryo processes, and a variant system has recapitulated YS blood formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C32 represent established knowledge about gastruloid models, supported by citations to prior literature. These claims provide essential background for the development of the haemGx model but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: The haemGx protocol successfully generates hemato-endothelial structures with time-dependent specification of VE-cadherin+C-Kit+ cells (120-144hr), CD41+ cells (144hr), and CD45+ cells (168hr onwards), with CD45+ cells forming cluster-like structures adjacent to endothelium. The protocol is reproducible across different mouse ES cell lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C42 are well-supported by experimental data including flow cytometry showing time-dependent marker expression (Figure 1C-D), imaging showing Flk1-GFP+ vascular networks and CD45+ clusters (Figure 1B, E), and reproducibility across cell lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F-I). The protocol design is clearly described with appropriate controls.

results.result: HaemGx cells display phenotypic characteristics of hematopoietic progenitors, with CD41+ and CD45+ cells co-expressing hemato-endothelial markers CD31 and CD34, and CD45+ cells expressing an HSPC-enriched phenotype (C-Kit+Flk1-GFP+VE-cadherin+) at ~1.8% frequency. Functional assays reveal >50 CFC/haemGx including ~7 multipotent GEM progenitors, with differentiated cells of multiple lineages present.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C49 are well-supported by flow cytometry data (Figure 2B-C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), CFC assays (Figure 2D-E), and cytospin analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A). The phenotypic characterization is thorough and the functional data numerically matches the estimated HSPC frequency, providing convergent evidence.

results.result: Gene expression analysis reveals sustained hemato-endothelial programs (Dll4, Mecom) and time-dependent hematopoietic patterns, with Myb peaking at 144hr (coincident with CD41+ cells), bimodal Runx1 expression (144hr and 216hr), and elevated Hoxa9/Hlf at 216hr, suggesting two distinct hematopoietic waves. EZH2 inhibition selectively reduces CD41+ cells at 144hr without affecting CD45+ cells at 216hr, supporting independent YS-like and AGM-like waves.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C55 are supported by qPCR data (Figure 2F) and EZH2 inhibition experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B-C). The temporal gene expression patterns align with known markers of YS and AGM hematopoiesis, and the differential sensitivity to EZH2 inhibition provides functional evidence for distinct waves. However, the interpretation relies on inference from marker expression and known biology rather than direct lineage tracing.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of 846 haemGx cells across timepoints identified 12 clusters, with clusters 0 and 5 mapping to C-Kit+ endothelial cells, cluster 4 capturing CD41+ cells with erythroid signature, and clusters 1 and 8 containing CD45+ cells with myeloid/lymphoid gene expression. Later timepoint clusters matched mesenchymal stromal and autonomic neuron signatures, suggesting incipient HSC niche formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C62 are supported by comprehensive scRNA-seq analysis with appropriate quality control (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C), clustering analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), and differential gene expression (Supplementary files 1-2). The cell type assignments are validated by marker expression and enrichment analysis. The sample size of 846 cells is modest but adequate for the analysis performed.

results.result: Focused scRNA-seq analysis of hemato-endothelial cells reveals time-dependent expression patterns consistent with YS-like and AGM-like hematopoiesis, with early endothelial markers (Pecam, Cd34, Mecom) in C-Kit+ cells, Runx1 in hematopoietic clusters, and AGM-associated markers (Cd44, Cdh5, Sox17, Procr) enriched at 192hr. Late timepoints show Hoxa9/Mllt3/Hlf expression in C-Kit+/CD45+ cells and increased Ikzf1 in CD45+ cells, with a shift from erythroid/megakaryocytic to myelo-lymphoid lineage affiliation between 144hr and 216hr.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C73 are supported by detailed scRNA-seq gene expression analysis (Figure 3B-E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) with appropriate statistical testing. The temporal patterns of marker expression align with known developmental hematopoiesis, though the interpretation of AGM-like characteristics relies on marker expression rather than functional validation. The detection of adult globins at 216hr (C73) provides additional support for definitive hematopoiesis.

results.result: Projection of haemGx scRNA-seq data onto published embryonic datasets positions endothelial clusters between E8.5-E10, with CD45+ cells mapping to E10 HE and intra-aortic clusters, CD41+ cells matching YS EMP identity, and a subset of CD45+ cells mapping to AGM IAC and FL LMPP, suggesting the presence of both YS-like and AGM-like progenitors in haemGx.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C79 are supported by projection analysis onto three independent published datasets (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 3) using appropriate computational methods (scmap with correlation threshold 0.7). The convergent mapping across multiple datasets strengthens the conclusions, though the interpretation relies on transcriptional similarity rather than functional equivalence. The analysis appropriately acknowledges the similarity between YS and AGM transcriptional programs.

results.result: HaemGx cells show limited engraftment potential when dissociated and transplanted, but undissociated haemGx implanted in the adrenal gland of nude mice demonstrate low-level short-term engraftment (<0.1% BFP+ cells) in bone marrow and spleen at 4-8 weeks, with erythro-myeloid lineages at 4 weeks and lympho-myeloid lineages at 8 weeks. Engraftment occurs without consistent adrenal enlargement, suggesting hematopoietic activity rather than teratoma formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C89 are supported by PCR detection of BFP in 3/5 recipients at 4 weeks (Figure 4C) and flow cytometry showing <0.1% BFP+ cells (Figure 4D-E). However, the engraftment levels are at the detection limit, with only 1 recipient showing multilineage engraftment at 8 weeks. The small sample size (n=5 at 4 weeks, n=4 at 8 weeks with 1 early sacrifice), low engraftment frequency, and lack of long-term engraftment limit the strength of conclusions. The interpretation that engraftment reflects different progenitor classes (C89) is speculative. Additional experiments with larger cohorts and functional validation are needed.

results.result: Infant AML transforms fetal liver but not adult hematopoietic cells, and MNX1-r patient transcriptional signatures show enrichment in cardiomyogenic, endothelial, HSC/progenitor, and mast cell signatures.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C91 are supported by citations to prior literature (C90) and GSEA analysis of patient transcriptomes (C91, Figure 5A). These claims provide essential background and rationale for the MNX1 overexpression experiments but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: MNX1 overexpression in haemGx results in normal Flk1-GFP activation and elongation kinetics but produces larger, more cellular haemGx with increased contractile structures from 192hr onwards and a small but significant expansion of C-Kit+ cells specifically at 144hr.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C94 are supported by imaging (Figure 5C), size quantification (Figure 5D), cellularity counts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), contractility observations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), and flow cytometry (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E). The statistical analysis shows significance for C-Kit+ expansion at 144hr (p=0.0191) but the effect size is modest. The data are consistent and reproducible across multiple experiments.

results.result: RNA-seq reveals distinct MNX1-driven transcriptional programs at 144hr and 216hr (>80% timepoint-specific genes), with 144hr showing upregulation of EHT/progenitor regulators (Runx1, Epor, Zfpm1) and enrichment of GATA2/GATA1/RUNX1 targets and VEGF/EMT pathways, while 216hr shows differentiated effectors (Hba-a1, Hbb-bh1, Il3ra) and cardiogenic enrichment without hemogenic TF enrichment.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C99 are supported by comprehensive RNA-seq analysis (Figure 5H-J, Supplementary file 4) with appropriate differential expression analysis, transcription factor binding site enrichment, and GO term enrichment. The temporal specificity of gene programs and the distinct regulatory signatures at 144hr vs 216hr provide strong evidence for selective targeting of YS-like hemogenic programs by MNX1. The analysis is thorough and well-controlled.

results.result: MNX1-OE transcriptomes show enrichment of haemGx HE cluster signatures (clusters 5 and 0) and YS-EMP-like cluster 4, and these HE signatures are also enriched in MNX1-r patient transcriptomes, aligning MNX1-OE effects with HE and the hemogenic transition.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C101 are supported by GSEA analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B-C) showing enrichment of haemGx cluster signatures in both MNX1-OE haemGx and patient samples. This provides important validation that the model recapitulates patient biology. However, the analysis relies on transcriptional similarity and the patient sample size for MNX1-r AML is not specified, which could affect the robustness of the comparison.

results.result: MNX1-OE haemGx cells from both 144hr and 216hr timepoints demonstrate serial replating capacity for at least 5 platings (significantly different from EV controls), with replated cells maintaining C-Kit+ phenotype and co-expressing CD31. Early replating enriches for Ter119+ erythroid cells, particularly from 144hr timepoint, but this is not sustained.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C105 are supported by serial replating assay data (Figure 6A-D) with appropriate statistical analysis and flow cytometry characterization (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C). The replating capacity is a classical indicator of transformation potential. However, the number of replicates varies (n=3-8) and the EV control shows some replating at 144hr, though significantly less than MNX1-OE. The phenotypic characterization is thorough.

results.result: RNA-seq of serially replated MNX1-OE cells shows increased human MNX1 expression and identifies cluster k14 of DEGs that are upregulated in both CFC replating and 144hr MNX1-OE haemGx. This k14 cluster shows significant enrichment of MNX1-r patient signatures against other AML subtypes, with cell type signatures capturing early hemogenic components (endothelial cells, erythroid precursors) and mast cells, reflecting YS EMP-like affiliation.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C111 are supported by RNA-seq analysis (Figure 7A-D) with hierarchical clustering, GSEA showing significant enrichment (Figure 7C), and cell type enrichment analysis. The convergence of k14 genes being upregulated in both replating and 144hr MNX1-OE, combined with enrichment of patient signatures, provides strong evidence for recapitulation of patient biology. The cell type analysis appropriately interprets mast cell affiliation as YS EMP-like based on recent literature (Chia et al., 2023).

results.result: Cytospin analysis of serially replated MNX1-OE cells shows progression from blast-like morphology at plate 3 to precursor cells with differentiated mast cells at plate 5 when initiated from 144hr, while 216hr-initiated colonies show earlier mast cell differentiation, suggesting maturation of MNX1-OE-responsive C-Kit+ progenitors between 144hr and 216hr.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113 are supported by cytospin analysis (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C) showing morphological progression. The interpretation that earlier differentiation in 216hr-initiated colonies reflects progenitor maturation (C113) is reasonable but relies on inference. The morphological analysis complements the molecular data and supports the temporal window of MNX1 susceptibility.

results.result: The haemGx model captures multi-wave blood formation, generates hematopoietic progenitors capable of short-term engraftment upon in vivo maturation, and when used to model MNX1-driven leukemia, promotes expansion and transformation of YS-like erythroid-myeloid progenitors that recapitulate patient transcriptional signatures.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C3, C5, and C6 represent the major conclusions of the manuscript. C2 is well-supported by the comprehensive phenotypic, functional, and transcriptional characterization across multiple timepoints. C3 is supported but with limitations due to low engraftment levels and small sample sizes. C5 and C6 are well-supported by the MNX1 overexpression experiments showing selective expansion at 144hr, serial replating capacity, and strong enrichment of patient signatures in the k14 cluster. The convergence of multiple lines of evidence (flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, functional assays, patient signature enrichment) provides robust support for the main conclusions, though the engraftment data remain the weakest component.

results.result: MNX1-driven leukemia represents the commonest genetic abnormality unique to the infant group.
results.evaluation: Claim C4 is supported by citation to prior literature on infant AML. This represents established knowledge that provides rationale for focusing on MNX1-r AML as a model system.

results.result: The haemGx model captures multi-wave blood formation through a differentiation protocol involving Activin A, VEGF, FGF2, and Shh, generating sequential populations of VE-cadherin+ C-Kit+ cells (120-144h), CD41+ cells (144h), and CD45+ cells (168-216h) with cluster-like structures adjacent to endothelium.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the protocol generates hematopoietic populations but express concern about the claim of capturing multiple waves. Reviewer 2 states 'it remains unclear whether the system recapitulates sequential waves of hematopoiesis or merely reflects the progressive maturation of cells originating from a single wave.' Reviewer 3 notes improvements but states 'the claim of "spatio-temporal accuracy" should be more cautiously phrased.'

results.result: Flow cytometry and functional assays demonstrate that haemGx generates endothelial cells (CD31+CD34+), hematopoietic cells with hemato-endothelial markers, AGM-like HSPC phenotype (CD45+ C-Kit+ Flk1-GFP+ VE-cadherin+, ~8 cells/haemGx), and >50 colony-forming cells including multipotent GEM progenitors.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the phenotypic characterization but question the interpretation. Reviewer 2 states 'The identification of lymphoid or pre-HSC-like populations is primarily inferred from scRNA-seq data. The lack of robust functional validation...significantly weakens the manuscript's main claims.' Reviewer 3 notes 'The case for YS-like EMP and AGM-like HSPC precursors is reasonably made, though further functional distinctions...would strengthen the claims.'

results.result: qPCR analysis shows temporal progression of hemato-endothelial markers with bimodal Runx1 expression (144h and 216h), Myb peaking at 144h coincident with CD41+ cells, and increased Hoxa9/Hlf at 216h suggesting AGM-like HSPC. EZH2 inhibition selectively reduces CD41+ cells at 144h but not CD45+ cells at 216h, supporting two independent waves.
results.evaluation: Reviewers question whether the data support distinct waves versus progressive maturation. Reviewer 1 critically notes 'it is evident from the UMAP provided that there is no HOXA9 expressed in either endothelium or blood cells. This argues very strongly against the proposition that AGM-type hematopoiesis is generated.' The EZH2 inhibition data is not specifically discussed by reviewers.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis identifies 12 clusters including endothelial (clusters 0, 5), CD41+ (cluster 4), and CD45+ (clusters 1, 8) populations. Gene expression analysis shows endothelial markers (Pecam, Cd34, Mecom), arterial markers (Flt1, Efnb2, Dll4), AGM-associated markers (Cd44, Sox17, Procr, Hoxa9, Hlf), and a shift from erythroid/megakaryocytic to myelo-lymphoid lineage affiliation between 144h and 216h.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the scRNA-seq data but express significant concerns about interpretation. Reviewer 1 states 'it is evident from the UMAP provided that there is no HOXA9 expressed in either endothelium or blood cells. This argues very strongly against the proposition that AGM-type hematopoiesis is generated.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the claim in line 263 that Cluster 8 (CD45⁺ cells at 192-216 h) expresses lymphoid markers is not clearly supported by the provided supplemental data.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'scRNA-seq re-clustering supports two hematopoietic waves with distinct marker sets' but notes 'further functional distinctions...would strengthen the claims.'

results.result: Projection of haemGx scRNA-seq data onto published embryonic datasets (Hou et al., Zhu et al., Thambyrajah et al.) shows that endothelial clusters map to E8.5-E10 HE, CD41+ cells map to YS EMP and some to IAC/HE, and CD45+ cells map to IAC, LMPP, and myeloid progenitors, suggesting presence of both YS-like and AGM-like progenitors.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the projection analysis as valuable but remain uncertain about the conclusions. Reviewer 2 states 'they do not test whether these cells might more closely resemble YS-derived EHT, which remains an unresolved and critical question' and concludes 'the current data do not support this conclusion and instead suggest that the system recapitulates the generation of multipotent lymphoid progenitors (MLPs) akin to those found in the YS.' Reviewer 3 notes 'Projection onto multiple embryonic reference datasets...is a valuable addition' but the interpretation remains cautious.

results.result: Direct transplantation of dissociated haemGx cells failed to engraft, but adrenal gland implantation of intact haemGx resulted in low-level (<0.1%) BFP+ engraftment in bone marrow and spleen of 3/5 recipients at 4 weeks (erythro-myeloid) and 1 recipient at 8 weeks (lympho-myeloid), suggesting short-term progenitor activity but incomplete functional maturation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers express significant concerns about the engraftment data. The editor states 'the claim of definitive wave hematopoietic progenitors being produced in the gastruloids, and their engraftment after transplantation, would benefit from further validation.' Reviewer 2 notes 'The engraftment data presented are not particularly convincing. It is unclear why the analysis was terminated at 8 weeks post-transplant, especially given that a minimum of 12 weeks is generally required.' Reviewer 3 states 'this in vivo result remains marginal and should be interpreted with caution. Crucially, this still does not demonstrate HSC-level repopulation capacity' but acknowledges 'the revised manuscript has softened the claims accordingly, now referring to "progenitor" activity rather than "pre-HSC."'

results.result: MNX1 overexpression in haemGx causes increased cellularity, contractile structures, and selective expansion of C-Kit+ cells at 144h. Transcriptional analysis shows distinct time-specific programs with hemogenic enrichment (GATA2, GATA1, RUNX1 targets) at 144h and cardiogenic enrichment at 216h. MNX1-OE transcriptomes enrich for haemGx HE cluster signatures and MNX1-r patient signatures.
results.evaluation: Reviewers generally accept the MNX1 overexpression effects on haemGx. Reviewer 3 states 'The MNX1 overexpression experiments are generally convincing in showing early expansion of a putative HE-to-EMP-like population and transcriptional resemblance to MNX1-r AML.' However, Reviewer 2 notes 'Given the uncertainties discussed above, the interpretability of the MNX1 overexpression study is limited' due to concerns about the underlying haemGx characterization.

results.result: MNX1-OE haemGx cells show serial replating capacity (>5 platings) with enrichment of C-Kit+CD31+ cells and early Ter119+ cells. RNA-seq of replated cells identifies cluster k14 with significant enrichment of MNX1-r patient signatures and cell-type signatures including endothelial cells, erythroid precursors, and mast cells. Cytospin analysis shows progression from blast-like to mast cell morphology.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not specifically critique the serial replating and transformation data. Reviewer 3 states 'The MNX1 overexpression experiments are generally convincing in showing early expansion of a putative HE-to-EMP-like population and transcriptional resemblance to MNX1-r AML. However, the evidence for transformation is still solely based on in vitro data and lacks any evidence of in vivo leukaemia engraftment.'

results.result: Enforced MNX1 expression in haemGx promotes expansion and in vitro transformation of yolk sac-like erythroid-myeloid progenitors at the HE-to-hematopoietic transition, faithfully recapitulating patient transcriptional signatures.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the transcriptional similarity to patients but note the lack of in vivo validation. Reviewer 3 states 'the evidence for transformation is still solely based on in vitro data and lacks any evidence of in vivo leukaemia engraftment. The ability to perturb the system would add translational value to the haemGx platform, although future studies are needed to better define transformation dynamics and leukemogenic progression.'

results.result: Current in vitro models of developmental blood formation lack spatio-temporal accuracy and weakly replicate successive waves of hematopoiesis.
results.evaluation: This background claim is not challenged by reviewers. Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'Gastruloids models are useful systems for studying early embryonic development' and Reviewer 2 notes 'The development of a novel in vitro system to model hematopoietic development is innovative and could potentially address important limitations of existing platforms.'

results.result: Background claims about embryonic hematopoiesis, pediatric leukemia, MNX1 biology, and gastruloid models.
results.evaluation: These background claims from the literature are not challenged by reviewers and serve to establish the scientific context for the study.

results.result: MNX1-driven leukemia represents the commonest genetic abnormality unique to the infant group, and infant AML transforms fetal liver but not adult hematopoietic cells.
results.evaluation: These background claims about infant AML are not challenged by reviewers and are supported by citations to prior literature.
